Model Experimentation, Selection and Monitoring

Overview

Agenda

  • [08:15 – 10:00] – Exercises: MLflow + warnings
  • [10:15 – 12:00] – Lecture: DORA metrics and model experimentation, selection and monitoring

Preparation

For the exercises:

  • https://MLflow.org/docs/latest/ml/ (use as reference material, don't do exercises)

For the lecture:

  • https://www.mlebook.com/wiki/doku.php (Chapter 9.3 + 9.4 + 9.5)
  • https://ml-ops.org/content/mlops-principles (Monitoring in particular)
  • https://www.datadoghq.com/knowledge-center/dora-metrics/ (or other DORA metric google searches is fine)
  • https://neptune.ai/blog/how-to-monitor-your-models-in-production-guide (skimming it is fine)
  • https://dvc.org/doc/use-cases/experiment-tracking (skimming it is fine)
  • Overview of different MLOps tools (skimming it is fine)

Notes

Lecture

The lecture uses the DORA metrics as the red thread for explaining why model experimentation, selection and monitoring is important:

  • Lecture Intro - Outline and the DORA metrics for MLOps
  • Working in a Team - Working on a technical product together
  • DORA Metrics - The four delivery metrics and their shortcomings
  • DORA for MLOps - What the metrics mean for ML systems
  • Deployment Frequency - What a deployment is for ML
  • Model Issues - Model decay, quantifying changes and drift
  • Data Issues - Data quality, drift and outliers
  • Logging - Log, monitor and alert for everything
  • Lead Time for Changes - What affects the speed of changes
  • Experimentation - Tracking ML experiments with MLflow and DVC
  • In Production - Selecting and promoting models
  • Mean Time to Restore - Restoring ML systems
  • MTTR: Causes - Troubleshooting and rolling back models
  • Change Failure Rate - What a failure is for ML
  • Managing Failures - Pilots, A/B tests and shadow testing
  • Summary - The DORA metrics revisited

Exercises

The following exercises will guide you through model experimentation:

  • Exercise 0: Installation - Install MLflow and dependencies
  • Exercise 1: Run an ML Experiment - Create and log ML experiments with MLflow
  • Exercise 2: Running a Custom Model - Define and use custom models
  • Exercise 3: Check Performance of Deployed Model - Monitor for data and concept drift

Note — Learning outcomes By the end of the exercises, we expect you to be able to do the following:

  • Organise ML experiments using common tools
  • Motivate how this can be used to deploy models
  • Explain how to detect concept and model drift

There are 4 python files in the resources folder for these exercises:

  • data_util.py, which you can use for generating the data (imagine it is the output of the data processing pipelines)
  • example_model.py, which you can use as the basic SKLearn model
  • basic_mlflow_training.py, which you can use to guide you on how to create a custom model/function and set up MLflow
  • basic_mlflow_evaluation.py, which you can use for evaluating the (created) models using new data and check for drifts.

As always for the most effective learning, try to use the MLflow documentation and figure out how to solve the exercises yourself first before consulting the basic MLflow scripts.
